glosses: Making good, thorough, or careful use of resources; not consuming extra. Especially, making good use of time or energy.

examples.text: An efficient process would automate all the routine work.
Our cleaners are almost too efficient: they throw away anything left out on a desk.

An artificial kidney these days still means a refrigerator-sized dialysis machine. Such devices mimic[…]real kidneys[…]. But they are nothing like as efficient, and can cause bleeding, clotting and infection—not to mention inconvenience for patients, who typically need to be hooked up to one three times a week for hours at a time.

glosses: Expressing the proportion of consumed energy that was successfully used in a process; the ratio of useful output to total input.

examples.text: The motor is only 20% efficient at that temperature.

glosses: Causing effects, producing results; bringing into being; initiating change (rare except in philosophical and legal expression efficient cause = causative factor or agent).

examples.text: Ownership, maintenance, or use of the automobile need not be the direct and efficient cause of the injury sustained
